canonicalise.note: Canonical form does not convert three-letter ISO 639-2 codes; only reading an old three-letter field does (legacy_three_letter).
A registered extlang replaces the language, and the language it leaves (ajp) is then replaced by its own Preferred-Value (apc).
An extlang the registry does not list is kept where it is.
Only space, tab, line feed and carriage return are trimmed; a no-break space makes the value malformed.
A digit is a valid single-character extension subtag.
A replacement that leaves the same variant twice drops the later one, so the result is stable.
Steps 4 and 5 repeat until stable: sgn-DD -> sgn-DE (region replaced) -> gsg (redundant tag replaced).
A line break inside the value is not trimmed; it makes the value malformed (a regular expression whose end anchor matches before a final line break would wrongly accept each part).

iso639_2_write.description: Two letters starting with q are not the local-use range qaa-qtz, which is three letters. qb has no ISO 639-2 code, so und is written, not qb.
Canonical form lower-cases QM to qm, which is still two letters and so still not a local-use code: und is written, not qm.

posix_locale.description: A leading no-break space (U+00A0) is not one of LANG-001's four whitespace characters, so it is not trimmed. It stays part of the value, which is then malformed, so there is no tag.

sidecar_name.description: A builder refuses 1: numbering starts at the second file
A builder refuses a negative number
A builder refuses more than nine digits, which a reader could not read back
A builder reads the language it is given with LANG-002's reader, so the old three-letter code fre is written as fr, which is what a reader reads back.
zzz is not in the ISO 639-2 table, not a registered subtag, not in the local-use range and not the XXX marker, so LANG-002's reader does not recognise it: the builder writes und.

canonical_order.description: Basic primary languages
Generic and regional English
Spanish: countries before the Latin America area code
Scripts
Script + region after script-only and region-only
The original language's whole group comes first
Within the original group, the item marked original leads
Two original languages: both groups first, in canonical order
Special codes after ordinary languages, in a fixed order
Malformed values last, in the order found
Ordering uses canonical forms
Equal tags keep their order
Variants and extensions after the plain forms
Serbian scripts and regions
Two- and three-letter codes compared as plain ASCII
Not by English name (which would give zh, de, el, ja)
zh-TW is region-only; it is not treated as zh-Hant-TW
A track marked original is promoted even when its language is not known
Each local-use code is its own group
An unregistered extlang counts as an additional subtag
A tag that merely ends in a private-use part is an ordinary tag. Its private-use part is kept when the tag is read, and LANG-021 rule 5 puts it after the plain tag of the same language.
Two tags that differ only in their private-use part are ordered by the rest of the tag as plain ASCII (LANG-021 rule 5).
A tag with a private-use part comes after every plainer tag of its group, however specific those are: script only, then region only, then the one with the private-use part (LANG-021 rule 5).

track_order.description: Types kept apart; roles ordered within a language
Original flags promote per track type
A track with several roles is placed by the latest of them
Role comes before variant within a language
An original audio track does not promote unmarked subtitles of the same language
Two malformed audio tracks keep the order they were found in. The first is commentary and the second has no role, but roles do not reorder malformed values among themselves (LANG-026).

presentation_order.description: The policy's own example: English interface, Japanese original, no preferences
Preferences first, in the user's order, then the original
A preference that is also the original is not listed twice
French interface: éwé sorts with the e's, not after z
German interface: order follows German names, not codes
An exact regional preference leads its group
Only exact preferences are promoted; en-GB is not promoted by en-US
A selection does not reorder the menu (same as present-06)
Roles within a group: main, then description, then commentary
Asking for audio description moves it ahead within its group
Special codes after all named languages, in their fixed order
Malformed values last
Two originals with no preferences
A preferred language that is not present is skipped
Asking for captions moves SDH ahead; forced stays after full
A regional preference brings the whole group forward
Several originals are ordered by localised name, not code
Asking for captions moves only tracks placed as SDH; a forced SDH track stays with forced
A preference may name a special code
An original of unknown language still comes first
A private-use preference promotes only its own tag
Malformed entries keep the order they were found in; roles and original flags do not reorder them
Groups whose localised names are identical (two named Malay, two named Norwegian) are ordered by primary language code, whatever order they were found in.

subtitle_menu.description: Off comes first and is not a language
Off is offered even with no subtitle tracks

label.description: A role listed twice appears once, and roles are still in TRACK-050's order.
An empty channel layout adds nothing to the label, not even a separator.
A role whose localised name is empty adds nothing to the label, not even a separator; the parts after it still follow.

match.description: Two malformed values match nothing, even when they are the same text apart from case.
An empty value is malformed, and a malformed value does not match even an identical one.

auto_select_audio.description: Exact preference wins
The general form beats a related one
Preference order comes before match strength
No preference matches: the original
No preference, no original: the default
Nothing else to go on: first in canonical order, not first in the list
Commentary is never chosen automatically while another track exists
…unless every track is special
Main programme before audio description when not asked for
Audio description first when the user asked for it
Role outranks match strength for a user who needs description
Two equal tracks: the identifier decides, not the list position
Nothing else to go on: a main track rather than description nobody asked for
An alternate mix ranks after the main programme
A track placed as "other" is never chosen while another exists
Malformed languages: the identifier decides, not the list position
Role rank uses the placing role: alternate + audio description is placed as audio description
Digits-only identifiers compare as numbers: 9 before 10
Equal as numbers, then plain text: 01 before 1
Two tracks with the same identifier: refuse rather than guess
A malformed preference matches nothing, not even a track with the same malformed text ignoring case, so selection falls through to the default track.

Canonical order counts every audio track, including ones that cannot be chosen. The original Japanese commentary is never chosen, but it still brings the Japanese group forward, so of the two default tracks the Japanese one comes first.

When every audio track is commentary or other, commentary ranks before other even though audio description was asked for. Role rank comes before the default flag and the identifier, which both favour the other track.
Identifiers made only of digits come before all others, compared as numbers of any length: a 40-digit identifier is still digits only, so it comes before 0abc.

auto_select_subtitle.description: Automatic, audio understood: the forced track in the audio's language
Automatic, audio understood, no forced track: nothing
Automatic, audio not understood: full subtitles, never a forced track
Captions asked for: SDH first
Always: a forced track is not full subtitles
Off means off
Forced only: a related variant of the audio's language counts
Forced only: unknown audio language, nothing to match
Automatic with no preferences acts as forced only
Always: no preference matches, so the default full track
A different script is never a match
Exact regional match first
The general form beats another region
Forced only: fewer removed subtags wins
No audio chosen: automatic acts as always when there are preferences
Always, no preference matches: the default among full subtitles, never a commentary track
Forced only with no audio chosen: nothing
Forced only: audio of unknown language with a script still matches nothing
Captions asked for: a forced SDH track is placed as forced and is never full subtitles
Two tracks with the same identifier: refuse rather than guess
Preferences that are all malformed count as none, so automatic mode acts as forced only: the forced English track matching the English audio, not the default full track.
A private-use audio tag has something to match in forced-only mode: a forced track with exactly that tag, not one with a different private-use tag.
A grandfathered audio tag with no replacement has something to match in forced-only mode: a forced track with exactly that tag.
